question: What is shadcn-vue and how is it different from a typical component library?
expected_answer: shadcn-vue is a collection of unstyled, accessible Vue components built on `reka-ui` primitives, distributed as copy-paste source code via the CLI. Unlike npm-installed component libraries, you own the component code in your repo and customize it freely. The CLI runs `npx shadcn-vue@latest add <component>` to add components to your project.

question: How do I install shadcn-vue in a Vite project?
expected_answer: Run `npx shadcn-vue@latest init` to scaffold `components.json` and the base styles. Configure Tailwind, then add components individually with `npx shadcn-vue@latest add <component>`. The Vite installation guide walks through the full setup including path aliases and `tailwind.config`.

question: How do I install shadcn-vue in a Nuxt project?
expected_answer: Run `npx shadcn-vue@latest init` from the Nuxt project root. Add `@nuxtjs/tailwindcss` to modules, configure `components.json` with the Nuxt path alias, and set up the `auto-imports` exclusion for the `~/components/ui` directory so the CLI-added components aren't double-registered.

question: What's in components.json and what does each field do?
expected_answer: `components.json` configures the CLI: `style` (default theme), `tailwind` (config path, css path, base color, prefix), `aliases` (`components`, `utils`, `ui`, `lib`, `hooks` paths), `iconLibrary` (lucide / etc), `framework` (vite / nuxt / astro / laravel). The CLI uses these when adding components.

question: How do I add a button to my project?
expected_answer: Run `npx shadcn-vue@latest add button` to copy the Button component into your project. Then `import { Button } from '@/components/ui/button'` and use `<Button variant="outline">` in templates. Variants: default, secondary, destructive, outline, ghost, link.

question: How do I build a form with shadcn-vue and vee-validate?
expected_answer: Use the form components (`Form`, `FormField`, `FormItem`, `FormLabel`, `FormControl`, `FormMessage`) which wrap vee-validate. Define a yup or zod schema, pass it via `validationSchema` to `useForm`, and bind fields with `<FormField v-slot="{ componentField }" name="...">`. The forms guide shows the full pattern.

question: How do I integrate TanStack Form with shadcn-vue components?
expected_answer: Use `@tanstack/vue-form` to manage form state and pair it with shadcn-vue inputs. The TanStack Form integration page documents the wrapper components and shows how to wire `field` props into `<Input>`, `<Select>`, and other shadcn-vue components.

question: How do I configure dark mode?
expected_answer: shadcn-vue uses CSS variables. Toggle dark mode by adding the `dark` class to the `<html>` element. The dark-mode pages document Vite, Nuxt, and Astro patterns — typically using `useColorMode` (or `@vueuse/core`) and respecting the user's system preference.

question: How do I customize the theme colors?
expected_answer: Edit the CSS variables in `src/assets/css/main.css` (or wherever the shadcn theme is installed). Variables follow the OKLCH palette: `--background`, `--foreground`, `--primary`, `--secondary`, `--muted`, `--accent`, `--destructive`, `--border`, `--input`, `--ring`. Change them to override the default theme.

question: How do I create a modal dialog?
expected_answer: Add the `dialog` component (`npx shadcn-vue@latest add dialog`). Use `<Dialog>` with `<DialogTrigger>`, `<DialogContent>`, `<DialogHeader>`, `<DialogTitle>`, `<DialogDescription>`, `<DialogFooter>`. Open state is controlled via `v-model:open` on `<Dialog>`. For confirmation dialogs use `<AlertDialog>` instead.

question: What's the difference between Dialog, AlertDialog, Sheet, and Drawer?
expected_answer: `Dialog` is a centered modal. `AlertDialog` is a Dialog variant for confirmations (no escape-to-close). `Sheet` slides in from a side (top/right/bottom/left). `Drawer` is the mobile-first slide-up panel. Pick based on the interaction: confirmations → AlertDialog, inline edit → Sheet, mobile gestures → Drawer.

question: How do I build a data table with sorting and filtering?
expected_answer: Use the `<DataTable>` component with `@tanstack/vue-table`. Define columns via `ColumnDef[]`, pass them and the data array to the table. Sorting via `getSortedRowModel`, filtering via `getFilteredRowModel`, pagination via `getPaginationRowModel`. The data-table page has a complete recipe.

question: How do I add a date picker?
expected_answer: Run `npx shadcn-vue@latest add date-picker`. The component composes `<Popover>` + `<Calendar>` internally. Bind the value with `v-model`. For a date range, use `<RangeCalendar>` or pass `mode="range"` to the underlying calendar.

question: How do I show toast notifications?
expected_answer: Add the `sonner` component (`npx shadcn-vue@latest add sonner`) — it's the recommended toast solution. Place `<Toaster />` once at the root of your app, then call `toast('message')` from anywhere. Variants: `toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.warning`, `toast.info`, `toast.promise`.

question: How do I build a dropdown menu with keyboard shortcuts?
expected_answer: Compose `<DropdownMenu>` with `<DropdownMenuTrigger>`, `<DropdownMenuContent>`, `<DropdownMenuItem>`. Use `<DropdownMenuShortcut>` (or render a `<Kbd>`) inside an item to display the shortcut. For grouped menus, wrap items in `<DropdownMenuGroup>` with `<DropdownMenuLabel>`.

question: How do I create a command palette (cmd+k)?
expected_answer: Use `<Command>` with `<CommandInput>`, `<CommandList>`, `<CommandEmpty>`, `<CommandGroup>`, `<CommandItem>`, `<CommandShortcut>`. Wrap in `<CommandDialog>` for the modal version that opens on cmd+k. The command page documents wiring up keyboard listeners and search filtering.

question: How do I build a sidebar navigation?
expected_answer: Use `<Sidebar>` with `<SidebarProvider>` at the root. The component supports `collapsible="icon"` for a collapsible icon-only mode, `<SidebarHeader>`, `<SidebarContent>`, `<SidebarFooter>`, `<SidebarMenu>`, `<SidebarMenuItem>`, `<SidebarMenuButton>`. Use `<SidebarTrigger>` to toggle from anywhere.

question: How do I add charts to my dashboard?
expected_answer: Run `npx shadcn-vue@latest add chart`. shadcn-vue's chart component wraps `unovis` for data visualization. Define data and config, pass them to `<ChartContainer>` with the appropriate chart type (`<ChartLine>`, `<ChartBar>`, `<ChartArea>`, `<ChartPie>`).

question: How do I add a tooltip to a button?
expected_answer: Wrap the trigger element in `<TooltipProvider>` (once per app), then use `<Tooltip>`, `<TooltipTrigger>`, `<TooltipContent>`. The `as-child` prop on `<TooltipTrigger>` passes the props through to the wrapped element so the button doesn't get a redundant nested wrapper.

question: How do I create a multi-step form wizard?
expected_answer: Use the `<Stepper>` component (`npx shadcn-vue@latest add stepper`) — it provides `<StepperItem>`, `<StepperTrigger>`, `<StepperIndicator>`, `<StepperTitle>`, `<StepperDescription>`, `<StepperSeparator>`. Drive the active step with `v-model:step`. Combine with conditional rendering of form fields per step.

question: How do I build a searchable select?
expected_answer: Use `<Combobox>` instead of `<Select>` when the user needs to type to filter. Compose `<ComboboxRoot>`, `<ComboboxAnchor>` with `<ComboboxInput>`, `<ComboboxList>`, `<ComboboxItem>`. The combobox page demonstrates value/display separation and async option loading.

question: How do I create an OTP input field?
expected_answer: Add the `input-otp` component. Use `<PinInput>` with `<PinInputGroup>`, `<PinInputSlot>` for individual digits, `<PinInputSeparator>` for visual breaks. Bind the value with `v-model` — receives the concatenated string. Configure `length`, `mask`, and `inputmode`.

question: How do I make a button toggle that visually persists state?
expected_answer: Use `<Toggle>` for a single on/off button or `<ToggleGroup>` (with `<ToggleGroupItem>`) for a set of mutually exclusive (`type="single"`) or multi-select (`type="multiple"`) toggles. Bind state with `v-model:pressed` (single) or `v-model` (group).

question: What loading-state components are available?
expected_answer: `<Spinner>` for indeterminate inline loading, `<Skeleton>` for placeholder boxes that match the final layout shape, and `<Progress>` for determinate progress (with a `value` prop). Use Skeleton during initial loads to reduce layout shift, Spinner inside buttons during submission, and Progress for known-duration tasks.

question: How do I build a navigation menu with submenus?
expected_answer: Use `<NavigationMenu>` with `<NavigationMenuList>`, `<NavigationMenuItem>`, `<NavigationMenuTrigger>` (the top-level link), `<NavigationMenuContent>` (the popover with submenu items), and `<NavigationMenuLink>` for inner links. Use `as-child` on `<NavigationMenuLink>` to wrap a `<RouterLink>` from vue-router.

question: How do I create a breadcrumb trail?
expected_answer: Use `<Breadcrumb>` with `<BreadcrumbList>`, `<BreadcrumbItem>`, `<BreadcrumbLink>`, `<BreadcrumbSeparator>`, and `<BreadcrumbPage>` for the current page. Wrap the link with `as-child` to compose with `<RouterLink>`.

question: How do I implement infinite scroll or pagination on a long list?
expected_answer: For pagination UI, use `<Pagination>` with `<PaginationList>`, `<PaginationFirst>`, `<PaginationPrev>`, `<PaginationListItem>`, `<PaginationNext>`, `<PaginationLast>` and `<PaginationEllipsis>`. For infinite scroll, combine `<ScrollArea>` with an intersection observer (e.g. `useIntersectionObserver` from VueUse).

question: How do I add a context menu (right-click menu)?
expected_answer: Wrap the target in `<ContextMenu>`, `<ContextMenuTrigger>`. Inside `<ContextMenuContent>`, compose `<ContextMenuItem>`, `<ContextMenuCheckboxItem>`, `<ContextMenuRadioItem>`, `<ContextMenuSub>` for nested menus. The trigger fires on right-click; pass `as-child` to wrap an existing element.

question: How do I create a resizable split-pane layout?
expected_answer: Use `<ResizablePanelGroup>` with `<ResizablePanel>` children separated by `<ResizableHandle>`. Set `direction="horizontal"` or `vertical`, and pass `default-size`/`min-size`/`max-size` to each panel. The component persists drag state internally.

question: How do I add a number-only input with min/max constraints?
expected_answer: Use `<NumberField>` with `<NumberFieldContent>`, `<NumberFieldDecrement>`, `<NumberFieldInput>`, `<NumberFieldIncrement>`. Pass `:min`, `:max`, `:step`, and bind `v-model` to a numeric ref. Internally clamps and steps the value on blur.

question: How do I configure path aliases for component imports?
expected_answer: Set `aliases` in `components.json`: `components`, `utils`, `ui`, `lib`, `hooks` mapped to your path aliases (typically `@/components`, `@/lib/utils`, etc.). The CLI uses these when generating files, so all generated imports follow your project's alias convention.

question: How do I use the JavaScript API to add components programmatically?
expected_answer: Import from `@shadcn/cli` (or run via npx): `import { add } from 'shadcn-vue/cli'`. The CLI is also scriptable from a Node script for monorepo orchestration. The javascript page documents the programmatic API and CI/CD recipes.

question: How do I create a custom registry of components?
expected_answer: Define a registry JSON file with `name`, `homepage`, and an array of `items` (each with `name`, `type`, `dependencies`, `files`). Host it on a public URL. Consumers use `npx shadcn-vue@latest add <url>/<name>` to fetch from your custom registry. The registry pages document the schema and hosting patterns.

question: What CLI commands does shadcn-vue support?
expected_answer: `npx shadcn-vue@latest init` — set up `components.json` and base styles. `add <component>` — install one or more components. `diff <component>` — show local diff vs upstream. `remove <component>` — delete an installed component. Pass `--cwd`, `--silent`, `--overwrite`, or specific framework flags as needed.

question: How do I migrate from the old v3 docs to v4?
expected_answer: v4 ships with Tailwind v4 (CSS variables in `@theme` blocks instead of the JS config), removes the `style` setting (only one style remains), and renames a handful of components. The legacy page documents v3 → v4 migration steps including the codemods.

question: How do I add an avatar with fallback initials?
expected_answer: Use `<Avatar>` with `<AvatarImage src="...">` and `<AvatarFallback>` containing the initials. The fallback renders if the image fails to load or while it's loading. Style with size classes on `<Avatar>` itself.

question: How do I show validation errors inline below an input?
expected_answer: Wrap the input in `<FormField>` with a `name` matching your validation schema. Pair with `<FormControl>` for the input slot, `<FormMessage>` to render the error. The `<FormMessage>` only renders when the field has an error.

question: How do I create a card with header, content, and footer?
expected_answer: Compose `<Card>` with `<CardHeader>` (which contains `<CardTitle>` and `<CardDescription>`), `<CardContent>` for the body, and `<CardFooter>` for actions. Use `<CardAction>` inside the header for top-right buttons.

question: How do I add a switch toggle for a setting?
expected_answer: Add the `switch` component (`npx shadcn-vue@latest add switch`). Bind state with `v-model:checked`. Pair with `<Label>` for an accessible name (use `for` on the label and a matching `id` on the switch).

question: How do I create a multi-select with tag display?
expected_answer: Use `<TagsInput>` with `<TagsInputItem>` (each tag renders inside) and `<TagsInputInput>` for the new-tag input. Bind `v-model` to a string array. The component handles backspace-to-remove and Enter-to-add.

question: How do I display a slider with two thumbs (range)?
expected_answer: Pass an array `v-model` to `<Slider>` with two values: `<Slider v-model:value="[20, 80]">`. The component renders two thumbs and supports `min`, `max`, `step`. For visual feedback, wire the displayed values to the model.

question: How do I show a progress bar that animates while loading?
expected_answer: Use `<Progress :model-value="value">` with `value` as a 0-100 number. For indeterminate loading, omit `model-value` or set it to `null` and rely on the styled animated stripe.

question: How do I implement keyboard navigation across a custom list?
expected_answer: Most shadcn-vue components inherit keyboard handling from `reka-ui` primitives (arrow keys to move, Enter to select, Esc to close). For custom lists, wrap with `<Command>` or `<DropdownMenu>` to inherit the same patterns. Or build manually with `tabindex="-1"` and a `keydown` handler.

question: What's the difference between Combobox and Select?
expected_answer: `<Select>` is a closed list of fixed options; the user picks one via mouse or keyboard arrows. `<Combobox>` adds a text input for filtering — the user can type to narrow the list. Use Select when the option set is small (<10), Combobox when filtering helps (>20 options or async loading).

question: How do I make components styleable per-project after install?
expected_answer: Once a component is added, its source lives in your repo (e.g. `@/components/ui/button/Button.vue`). Edit it directly: change classes, add variants via `class-variance-authority`, restructure markup. Since it's your code, there's no upstream override mechanism — you own it.

question: How do I add an aspect ratio container for an image or video?
expected_answer: Use `<AspectRatio :ratio="16/9">` to wrap the media. The component maintains the ratio at any width. Common ratios: `16/9` (video), `1/1` (square), `4/3` (legacy video), `21/9` (cinemascope).

question: How do I show typography that matches the shadcn style?
expected_answer: The typography page documents standardized text styles: H1-H4 with consistent leading and tracking, blockquote, ul/ol with markers, inline code with a styled background, lead paragraph, large/small/muted modifiers. Apply via Tailwind classes or by composing the recommended HTML structures.

question: How do I install in an Astro project?
expected_answer: Add the Vue integration to Astro (`npx astro add vue`), then run `npx shadcn-vue@latest init` and pick the Astro framework option. Components live under `src/components/ui/`. Astro-specific notes: only client-side components (`client:load` etc) need full hydration; static usage is fine.

question: How do I install in a Laravel project?
expected_answer: Use Inertia.js + Vue. Add Vue via `npm install vue@next @vitejs/plugin-vue`, configure Vite to use the plugin, then run `npx shadcn-vue@latest init` and pick the Laravel framework option. Components install under `resources/js/components/ui/`.

question: How do I use shadcn-vue components with TypeScript?
expected_answer: All components ship with `.vue` SFCs that have TypeScript-ready scripts and proper prop types via Reka UI's interfaces. Imports are typed automatically. For passing props, use `defineProps<MyProps>()` patterns and rely on the auto-generated types from each component's `index.ts` re-exports.
